findings.text: The retrieved evidence supports suitcase detections temporally overlapping Shoplifting hypotheses in four windows: 36.267s-38.267s, 49.067s-51.067s, 51.2s-53.2s, and 55.467s-57.467s. The surveillance-event model produced a Shoplifting hypothesis in each, with co-occurring garbage collecting hypotheses. This is source agreement only and does not confirm an event or involvement.

The available evidence indicates other supplied windows do not meet both criteria: f16, f27 and f28 show Shoplifting hypotheses without suitcase detection; f18, f19 and f22 show suitcase detections with Burglary hypotheses rather than Shoplifting.

The retrieved evidence supports persistence of compatible hypotheses across adjacent windows: Shoplifting with suitcase and garbage collecting from 49.067s to 53.2s, and Shoplifting with person detections from 55.467s to 61.733s with suitcase only in the first window of that sequence.

limitations: Model labels such as Shoplifting, Burglary and garbage collecting are hypotheses, not confirmed crimes or actions.
A person detection temporally overlapping a hypothesis does not mean the person was involved.
